content:
Zane: Orbit onboarding flagged a weird churn: browsers are spamming OPTIONS (CORS) to /api/preflight and those are counted in our warmup quota. Customer sees 429s during rollout. Can someone take a look?
Priya: thanks. Two obvious contributors: they send a custom header (x-client-id) on every request from the page + the service worker also forwards the same header on fetch events. Custom headers trigger browser preflight (OPTIONS) which our warmup metrics currently count.
Zane: ah, so the browser OPTIONS are inflating request counts. Is there a mitigation that doesn't force them to remove client id?
Marta: couple of practical options (ordered by friction):
1) Server-side: set Access-Control-Allow-Headers to include x-client-id and add Access-Control-Max-Age: 600. That makes the browser cache the CORS preflight for 10 minutes, drastically reducing OPTIONS frequency. Example response header: `Access-Control-Max-Age: 600`.
2) Client-side: avoid sending custom headers on the hot path. Move client id into a URL query param or encode it in the ephemeral token payload so you can keep attribution without triggering preflight. E.g. `fetch(`/api/preflight?client=orbit-web-1`)`.
3) Service-worker change: only forward the preflight for background sync if no visible client/tab has warmed; use `clients.matchAll()` to check.
4) Short infra option: a 12h warmup throughput bump while they roll out these changes.
Zane: can you paste their current fetch pattern?
Orbit-Eng: simplified repro they sent:
```js
// main.js
fetch('/api/preflight', {
  method: 'POST',
  mode: 'cors',
  headers: {
    'authorization': `Bearer ${token}`,
    'x-client-id': 'orbit-web-1',
    'x-app-version': '1.3.2'
  }
});
// service-worker.js
self.addEventListener('fetch', evt => {
  if (shouldWarm(evt.request)) evt.respondWith(fetch(evt.request));
});
```
Marta: POST + custom headers = preflight every time unless cached by the browser. Since they also send x-app-version (another custom header) it's worse. Two immediate asks we gave them: change preflight to GET or POST without custom headers (or move attribution to query string), and set server Access-Control-Max-Age.
Priya: we advised them to try server header first because it's usually the fastest deploy on their stack. They patched and rolled; we also suggested moving x-client-id to query param to avoid future surprises.
Zane: OnboardBot, can you open a warmup ticket (12h) while they roll?
OnboardBot: Created ticket #ORBIT-ONB-11 for temporary warmup capacity (12h), owner: Marta, ETA: 1h.
Orbit-Eng: deployed Access-Control-Max-Age: 600 and moved client to query param for the preflight call. We also gated SW warmup using clients.matchAll().
Marta: early metrics after change: OPTIONS count dropped ~86% and 429s during warmup went from spikes to occasional single-digit retries. Sample logs:
[2026-10-14T10:02:00Z] OPTIONS orbit-web-1 200 cached
[2026-10-14T10:02:12Z] POST preflight 429 warmup-peak
[2026-10-14T10:02:40Z] POST preflight 200 retry-backoff
Zane: excellent. CS handoff checklist for Orbit: ["set Access-Control-Max-Age >= 600","avoid custom headers on hot path (move client id to query or token)","change POST->GET if possible for preflight endpoint","debounce SW preflight with clients.matchAll()","ops temp bump ORBIT-ONB-11, monitor 12h"].
Priya: also suggested a small SDK helper we can offer: a preflight wrapper that encodes client id into the token or query param and exposes a SW-safe guard. They asked for it.
Marta: I'll own the SDK patch if they want it. Closing once 12h monitoring shows stable warmup. :white_check_mark:
